claim: R3-10 ends a disaster's ruined look building by building: once a Works other than a `decay` Works has begun on a building, V06 §3.22 (3)'s `crisisLookYields` is true and the look leaves that building. V03 §5.6 (4) (l. 2722–2734: a building draws the look only while 'not yet handed over'; `PlanDamage.level` falls to the own level, `PlanDamage.look` to null), V10 §3.9a (l. 1852–1855: 'each until its rebuilding Works begins') and §3.9b (8), §10.2 (f), §8.2 and V02 §5.7 (1) all take it. V09 decides by district alone: §4.21.13 (3) (l. 3668–3672: 'In a district a disaster look ruins, the plan panel … shows the building's lines at the look's `lookLevel` … under the head `info.crisis.ruinedFor`'), §4.21.12 (4) (l. 3604–3609) and §5.8 (l. 3952–3953) give 'a building in a district a disaster look ruins' the why card's 'For now: {look}, {condition}, weeks {a}–{b}' row, and §1b's and §2.12's damage-lines rows (l. 378, 1008) read the look's `lookLevel` 'over the look's `districts`'; row 92 and T-V9-86 test no building under its rebuild. So for a building of a struck district whose rebuild Works has begun — the normal path of the `reconstruction` condition that is the look's own source (R3-09) — V09 lists ruin lines at `lookLevel` and calls it ruined for now, while V03 draws its plan at its own level, V02 and §8.2 draw it under scaffolding and V10 tells the user the look has left it: two members, two outcomes for one case.
required_change: V09 §4.21.13 (3): 'On a building a disaster look stands over — one of the look's `districts` (§11.2's `looks` reader), not yet handed over to a Works (V06 §3.22 (3)'s `crisisLookYields`, read through V03's `planDamage`: `PlanDamage.look` set; a preview never hands over) — the plan panel shows its lines at `PlanDamage.level` (the look's `lookLevel` by severity, or its own level where higher) under the head `info.crisis.ruinedFor`; once handed over it shows its own lines and head (V09 §4.21.13 (1))', the rest as it stands. V09 §4.21.12 (4) and §5.8: the `facts` row `info.crisis.ruinedFor` is given to 'a building a disaster look stands over (one of its `districts`, not yet handed over, V06 §3.22 (3); V03 §5.6 (4))'. §1b's and §2.12's damage-lines rows name `PlanDamage.look` as the input. §3.16 row 92 adds 'a building of a struck district whose rebuild Works has begun → its own level's lines and head, no `info.crisis.ruinedFor`'. T-V9-86 adds that clause on T-V3-40's (or T-V6-75's) fixture, a rebuild begun on one building of the district.

claim: V09 §4.21.13 (1) (l. 3649–3651) glosses the damaged set as '§6.3 *Plan damage*'s comparison — an element shows damaged while the building's decay level is above 0 and at least its threshold t'. It omits §2.6 step 7's one case with no threshold (R3-05): while a building is `decayed` or `ruined`, every roof bay over a room of a wing whose `RoofSpec.kind` is `none` is damaged whatever its t. V10 §3.9a states the case (l. 1821–1822, and its kind row), and V03's `planDamage`, which V09's lines read, carries it (V03 §5.6 (2) (c)). For a roofless decayed wing below a bay's t, V09's text gives no `roofBay` line and V10's rows give one. Nothing built changes (V09's lines are V03's layer); only the gloss is narrower. Same omission as VDC3-02 at §6.3; one fix with it.
required_change: V09 §4.21.13 (1), after '(a level of 0 damages nothing, so a never-decayed building draws its plan unchanged)': '; and, while the building is `decayed` or `ruined`, every roof bay over a room of a roofless wing (`RoofSpec.kind` `none`) whatever its threshold (§2.6 step 7)'.

claim: Find's Go there now writes the edit log. Round 3 changed V09 §4.2's working-layer switch from '(§7.8's layer controls, view state only)' to '(§7.8's layer controls: `LayerSpec.visible`, written by `setLayer`, §8.4)', and V09 row 21 to 'switching the working layer turns its visibility on (by `setLayer`, §8.4)'. This follows the layers-shown ruling: `LayerSpec` is document style state, and a toggle is a logged `setLayer` (§11.3; §7.4's setLayer row: log, inverse). Find's Go there runs that switch. V09 §4.21.10 (8): 'Below sets the working layer to Below and `depthBand` to the match's band (V04 §5.1); Sky sets it to Sky, the island menu's `key` to the match's island and a hidden sky layer visible (V05 §5.6 (3))'. V05 §5.6 (3) (l. 2319): 'Go there turns its visibility on, as switching the working layer does'. The underground layer is hidden by default at every rung (§8.4; V04 §5.1). So the common path is a chip with matches Below, then 'N more Below', then Go there, and it sends a logged, undoable `setLayer` into the document's style state and its edit log. That contradicts the owner rule, item 120 (a): 'Find never changes the model, the document, its hash or the edit log'. It also contradicts the base's Find tool (§9.5, l. 14951-14954): 'It sends no event and changes no model, document, hash or log … Go there sets the working layer and band (V04 §5.1, V05 §5.6) — view changes'. And it contradicts V04 §5.1 (2): Go there sets `depthBand`, 'a view key, never an edit'. A builder of V09 implements the contradiction.
required_change: V09 §4.21.10 (8): Go there sets view keys only. These are `workingLayer` (without §4.2's visibility write), `depthBand` for Below (V04 §5.1) and the island menu's `key` for Sky; then it flies. Where the target layer's `LayerSpec.visible` is false, Go there leaves the layer hidden and keeps its ghost pins and count. Beside the count it offers that layer's own visibility toggle, §7.8's layer control: the user's logged `setLayer`, §8.4. Find sends no event (item 120 (a); §9.5). V09 §4.2's 'Switching layer also sets the layer's visibility on' reads 'Switching layer in the view bar also sets the layer's visibility on … (never Find's Go there, V09 §4.21.10 (8))'. V05's END, §5.6 (3): 'and Go there turns its visibility on, as switching the working layer does' → 'and Go there leaves it hidden, offering its visibility toggle (a logged `setLayer` the user sends; V09 §4.21.10 (8)); Find sends no event (item 120 (a))'. T-V9-83 adds: Go there to a hidden Below and to a hidden sky layer logs 0 events and leaves the document's style unchanged. If the adjudicator rules another form, every Find action must still send no logged event.

claim: R3-21's END for V09 §4.2 (l. 1652–1653) makes the working-layer switch write the document: 'Switching layer also sets the layer's visibility on (§7.8's layer controls: `LayerSpec.visible`, written by `setLayer`, §8.4)'. `setLayer` is a logged, undoable style event (§7.4). Find's Go there works through that switch: V09 §4.21.10 (8) (l. 3514–3516: 'Below sets the working layer to Below …; Sky sets it to Sky, … and a hidden sky layer visible'); V05 §5.6 (3) (l. 2319: 'Go there turns its visibility on, as switching the working layer does'); T-V9-83 (g) ('a hidden sky layer shown'). The underground is hidden by default at every rung (II.7.1, D-3), so the common case, Go there on a Below match, now appends a `setLayer` to the edit log. This contradicts owner item 120 (a) ('Find never changes the model, the document, its hash or the edit log'), §9.5's Find ('It sends no event and changes no … log … Go there sets the working layer and band — view changes'), V09 §4.21.10 (1) and V04 §5.1 ('a view key, never an edit'). T-V9-83 (g) and (i) ('the log unchanged by Find') cannot both pass. A viewer may never edit (§11.3 Roles; §11.2 `edit` is an editing role's call), so a viewer's working-layer switch, or Go there to a hidden layer, needs an event its role cannot send, and no outcome is defined. Before this round V09 called the visibility 'view state only', and the paths did not meet. Grade: an owner rule contradicted where a builder following V09 and V05 would implement it, on a common path; at the least MAJOR (a bar that cannot pass).
required_change: Keep visibility as document style state, written only by a deliberate T12 `dress` toggle (R3-21); neither Find nor a viewer writes it. (1) V09 §4.2: 'Switching layer also sets the layer's visibility on (§7.8's layer controls: `LayerSpec.visible`, written by `setLayer`, §8.4) and dims the other layers to 35 % opacity.' → 'Switching layer dims the other layers to 35 % opacity and writes nothing to the document. A layer whose `LayerSpec.visible` is false (§8.4: document style state, written only by T12 `dress`'s logged `setLayer`) stays hidden, and the switch shows `info.layer.hidden` ("{layer} is hidden on this map."). For a role that may write style (owner, editor; §11.3), it also offers **Show it** — T12 `dress`'s toggle, `setLayer { layer, spec: { visible: true } }`, its own undo step. A viewer gets no **Show it**.' (2) V09 §4.21.10 (8): 'Sky sets it to Sky, the island menu's `key` to the match's island and a hidden sky layer visible (V05 §5.6 (3))' → 'Sky sets it to Sky and the island menu's `key` to the match's island — view keys only, never a `setLayer` (item 120 (a)). On a hidden layer the flight lands on its ghost pins with V09 §4.2's `info.layer.hidden` and its **Show it**, which is T12 `dress`'s edit, not Find's.' (3) V09 §3.16 row 21's outcome 'switching the working layer turns its visibility on (by `setLayer`, §8.4)' → 'the layer stays hidden, with `info.layer.hidden` and, for an owner or editor, **Show it** (a logged `setLayer`); a viewer's switch writes nothing'. (4) T-V9-83 (g): '(a hidden sky layer shown)' → '(on a hidden layer `info.layer.hidden`, no event logged)'; (i) stands. (5) V09 §4.9 adds the row `info.layer.hidden`. (6) END at V05 §5.6 (3): 'and Go there turns its visibility on, as switching the working layer does' → 'and Go there leaves its visibility as it stands (V09 §4.2: visibility is document style, which only T12 `dress`'s `setLayer` writes), the flight landing on its ghost pins'.

claim: V09's crisis card, why lines, legend entries and Find list read §11.2's `looks` reader, 'the one evaluation `live.crises` draws'. §8.2 re-runs that evaluation 'when the week crosses a condition's edge …, the crisis display or the key changes, the model the view draws changes (a commit, or the week crossing to another frame)'. V09 §2.12's rows re-read it on fewer triggers: l. 1005 (card and lines) 'rebuilt at each week change, absorb and `onEffectiveKey`' — no `crises` change, no commit; l. 1008 (damage lines, whose plan-panel look lines read the look's `districts` and `lookLevel`) — no `crises` change. Two normal paths diverge. Preview a crisis, or Show crises off, changes `crises`: the map draws the new looks while the card, Find's list and the plan panel keep the old ones, though V09 §4.21.12 (2) and (4) promise the preview's line. A commit that splits or merges a struck district changes a disaster's units 'at that commit' (V01 §3.16): the map draws the new districts while the card's `facts` row and the plan panel's look lines keep the old list until the next week change. One builder follows the row, another §8.2.
required_change: V09 §2.12 l. 1005: 'rebuilt at each week change, absorb and `onEffectiveKey`' → 're-read whenever the evaluation §8.2's `live.crises` runs changes: each change of §2.9's `week` or `crises` (**Show crises**, **Preview a crisis**), each `doc.changed` (a commit, an absorb, an undo or redo, a regenerate — an edit that splits or merges a struck district changes a disaster's units at that commit, V01 §3.16) and each `onEffectiveKey`'. l. 1008 adds '; for the plan panel's look lines, at each re-read of §11.2's `looks` reader (the row above)'. T-V9-85 adds: a preview picked and the switch turned off with the card open each update the card and Find's list at once, and a district split on a dossier fixture with a disaster standing updates the card's `facts` row at that commit.
